message.content:
Here is the proof.
The decision problem is clearly in NP.
We reduce from the classic integer subset sum decision problem.
Given subset sum numbers, build a star graph with weighted leaf edges only.
Set all vertex weights to zero, and set each given leaf edge weight to one number.
A subgraph chooses any edges, so its total weight always equals the sum of all chosen leaf edge weights.
Thus the constructed graph has a target weight subgraph exactly when some given positive integer numbers sum to the given target value.
Because membership and polynomial hardness both hold, the weighted graph subgraph decision problem is therefore NP complete for arbitrary integer weights on vertices and edges.
